The issue is that when `contains_over_clause` is true, the annotation mask logic masks out the window annotation, so the outer query references the window function directly.

The upstream fix (Django ticket #34717) added `contains_over_clause` to the subquery condition. But the annotation masking must keep the referenced window annotation. Let me look at the actual upstream patch logic — the key part is that when the query contains an over clause, the referenced window annotations must be selected in the inner query.

But the problem is the window annotation is added to `inner_query.annotations` via the mask, yet the outer query's aggregate still references it via `Ref`...
